sentences.text: Overtaking signals split the same way.
Look at the three International signals on screen.
They’re used in a narrow channel or fairway, when the vessel ahead has to help you get by.
Two prolonged blasts, then one short: I intend to overtake you on your starboard side.
Two prolonged, then two short: I intend to overtake you on your port side.
The two long blasts say overtaking.
The short ones are the same one for starboard and two for port.
And if the vessel ahead agrees, she answers: prolonged, short, prolonged, short.
Now the Inland version, which is simpler.
It applies between power-driven vessels in sight of one another in any waters, not just channels.
One short blast: I intend to overtake you on your starboard side.
Two short blasts: on your port side.
The vessel being overtaken answers with the same signal if she agrees, or the danger signal if she doesn’t.
